chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from whom he mentioned from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding
a man who slept through the ‘Atmah (late night prayer) and did not wake up until after midnight. He said: He performs it and remains fasting until morning.

key_terms.الْعَتَمَةِ: The late night prayer (Salat al-‘Atamah), typically referring to the two rak'ahs of Nafl prayed before Fajr or after Isha.
key_terms.انْتِصَافِ اللَّيْلِ: Midnight, the middle of the night period.
key_terms.يُصْبِحُ صَائِمًا: He becomes morning in a state of fasting, indicating the fast remains valid despite missing the prayer.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who misses the late night prayer due to sleep and wakes up after midnight?
ai.summary: In this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the involuntary nature of the sleep is distinguished from negligence, allowing the missed 'Atah (late night) prayer to be performed without invalidating the day's fast. This highlights the Shia juristic principle that the validity of acts of worship is preserved when the omission is due to a valid excuse like sleep, reflecting the divine ease (yusr) in Islamic law. The hadith underscores the importance of making up missed obligatory prayers even when they fall within the time of the next prayer cycle.
